summary: @or-sdk/queue-manager preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated 727 KB payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. On `npm install`, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into an OS temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses that Bun binary to execute the bundled sibling file `math_init.js` — a single-line 727 KB `@bun-cjs` bundle whose program is reconstructed at runtime from a large numeric/string lookup table `n7gIxM` via an array-rotation function `WV8StW` and a per-character decoder `hc1jfK9` keyed on a scrambled alphabet. No URLs, imports, or human-readable identifiers survive in the payload; behavior is only observable by executing it. The alternate-runtime delivery causes the payload to run under Bun rather than Node, so Node-oriented install-phase inspection does not see it. A queue-manager library has no functional need for a second language runtime at install time or for an opaque, heavily obfuscated auto-executed payload. CHANGELOG entries link to an internal-only host (`gitlab.internal.onereach.io/onereach/platform/or-sdk-next/...`) while the package is published on the public npm registry under `@or-sdk/queue-manager`, consistent with a dependency-confusion / name-hijack shape against an internal SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
